description: Capacity-hoarding indicators on EUA Carbon Dec-26 Future-linked transmission nominations are being assessed to determine whether withholding influenced observed price formation.
Collateral and margin reporting fields for German Power Baseload Day-Ahead were found complete and consistent following a targeted review; no further action was required.
Transaction reports for UK Power Baseload Day-Ahead contained an invalid national client identifier for one participant, requiring correction of static data and resubmission.
Order-to-trade ratios on German Power Baseload Day-Ahead for one algorithmic participant exceeded venue guidance, prompting a review of the strategy's messaging behaviour and its market impact.
A valuation-reporting discrepancy on EUA Carbon Dec-27 Future contracts between internal marks and the reported mark-to-market values requires reconciliation and possible amendment.
Clock-synchronisation records for THE Gas Calendar-27 order events showed drift beyond the permitted tolerance during one session, undermining sequencing evidence.
A marking-the-close concern on EUA Carbon Dec-26 Future is being assessed where a cluster of trades near the settlement window may have influenced the reference price.
Best-execution monitoring on TTF Gas Day-Ahead showed acceptable outcomes overall; a handful of outliers were explained by fast-market conditions and documented accordingly.

A suspected cross-market manipulation link between UK Power Baseload Season Win-26 and a related contract was investigated and closed after analysis showed the price relationship was consistent with normal arbitrage.
A fundamental-data publication error affecting EUA Carbon Dec-27 Future was corrected promptly and the corrected figures disseminated; no evidence of exploitation was found.

Trade repository reconciliation identified mismatched notional values on a set of German Power Peakload Cal-27 derivative contracts between the two counterparties, requiring bilateral correction of the reported figures.

An inside-information disclosure obligation for a planned outage affecting UK Power Baseload Day-Ahead was met, though publication was nine minutes late. Process timing was tightened to ensure timely disclosure.

Potential wash-trade pattern flagged where a participant appeared on both sides of several THE Gas Month-Ahead Aug-26 transactions within a short window, producing no change in beneficial ownership. Surveillance opened a review to establish intent and economic rationale.
Suspected mis-tagging of TTF Gas Month-Ahead Aug-26 orders as liquidity-providing when they were aggressive is being examined, as it affects fee treatment and surveillance classification.
A benchmarking review of TTF Gas Option Sep-26 price submissions found the contribution process robust, with adequate governance and record-keeping in place.

Transaction reporting completeness check found a small number of Nordic Power System Day-Ahead trades reported after the T+1 deadline due to a feed delay. Late reports were resubmitted and a control added to the reporting pipeline.
Position-limit monitoring confirmed that French Power Baseload Cal-27 exposures remained within regulatory thresholds throughout the period; near-limit alerts were reviewed and cleared.
An abnormal trading-volume alert on Nordic Power Baseload Q4-26 was investigated and attributed to a legitimate portfolio rebalancing by a large participant; the case was closed with a note.
Missing unique trade identifiers on a batch of TTF Gas Option Sep-26 contracts blocked pairing at the trade repository. The reporting party is regenerating identifiers and resubmitting.

A momentum-ignition concern on German Power Baseload Cal-27 arose where aggressive trading appeared timed to trigger other participants' stops. Order and trade sequencing is under detailed reconstruction.
Late confirmation of TTF Gas Month-Ahead Aug-26 bilateral trades was remediated and the confirmation workflow automated to prevent recurrence.

Spoofing indicators triggered on NBP Gas Month-Ahead Aug-26 where sizeable orders were repeatedly entered and withdrawn on one side while the participant traded on the other. The pattern is being examined against benign explanations.

Unusual price movement in French Power Baseload Cal-27 shortly before a fundamental market announcement prompted an insider-dealing screen. Trading records and communications are being reviewed for the relevant participants.

A sequence of layering-like orders on Nordic Power System Day-Ahead was detected, with large non-genuine orders placed away from the touch and cancelled before execution. Analysts are assessing whether the activity was manipulative or legitimate liquidity provision.
Communications review linked to UKA Carbon Dec-26 Future activity flagged ambiguous language between traders; the context is being clarified to rule out coordinated behaviour.
